newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 4.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
*Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says the 1997 budget can be modified. Prime minister Romano Prodi agrees:"It can be altered but not distorted" (all).
* The Freedom alliance unveils a "counter-budget" proposal which aims to cut the deficit by 62.1 trillion lire (all).

* In a row with communist Refoundation party, Massimo D'Alema, leader of the Democratic party of the Left, warns that if a government crisis breaks out over the budget in Parliament, there will be new elections (Corriere della Sera, Repubblica).
* French President Jacques Chirac starts a two-day visit in Italy and makes peace with Prime minister Romano Prodi (all).

* Metal workers threaten to stage a new national strike over their contract renewal as Giorgio Fossa, chairman of the employers association, says "under these conditions the metal workers contract is unacceptable"(all).

*In a meeting with financial analysts, Olivetti chief executive officer Roberto Colaninno said he planned to divest Olivetti's ailing PC business and three other units by the end of the year. Divestments would allow the group to raise 800 billion lire (all).
* As the lira hits new highs against the deutsche mark breaking the 990 level, Italian manufacturers start worrying they might loose their competitiveness (Sole 24 Ore).
* Stocks in state energy group ENI slip 2.47 per cent at the Milan stock exchange. A second tranche of the company is due to be floated at the end of the month (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
